values: Airbus EASA AD duplicate review — document-level verdicts

Manual review of 14 same-version conflict rows and 17 near-duplicate pairs. Source PDFs were checked for their own header number, Date/Issued field, subject/applicability, and explicit Supersedure/Revision wording. Google Drive source data was not modified.

No reviewed file is a duplicate to delete.

The 14 conflict rows are seven false groups created by seven wrong AD-number parses.

All 17 similarity pairs are valid historical/parallel relationships; keep both PDFs in every pair.
Seven legacy successor/follow-on PDFs were assigned an older referenced AD number; the paired PDFs are distinct and all must remain.
Thirteen are explicit direct supersedures, one is a revised-successor lineage, one is transitive, and two are companion ADs.
Do not turn companion or transitive similarity pairs into direct links. Preserve the two direct galley edges and exclude the two-hop shortcut.
This workbook records the review. It does not rewrite the manifest, reports, or source PDFs.

values: Parser correction exposed by the seven false conflict groups
The source PDFs are correct. The current AD_HEADER_RE fails on legacy headers with spaces around the dash, then accepts an older compact body reference as if it were the document's own AD number.
Own headers use forms such as 2007 - 0281 or 2008 – 0032.
The current year-separator-number pattern does not allow surrounding spaces, so the correct header is skipped.
Later text contains compact references such as EASA AD 2006-0047.
Because No. is optional, a body reference satisfies AD_HEADER_RE and is returned with 1.00 confidence.
Require AD No. for the high-confidence header regex and anchor it to a line on page 1.
All seven affected filenames encode the correct AD number, but the older body match overrides them.
Seven unrelated files are grouped under old logical-version keys, producing 14 conflict rows.
Parse header and filename independently; if they disagree, flag the row and prefer the anchored own-header/filename consensus.
AD bodies legitimately cite many earlier ADs.
A generic first-page number is not safe as a current-document identifier.
Use generic matching only after both header and filename fail, and keep low confidence/manual review.
The PDFs and extracted text did not change; only parsing/grouping logic changes.
Recompute AD enrichment and manifest fields
Cached records must be re-enriched with the new regex before duplicate grouping.
Each corrected row moves to its own true AD family.
The source says Supersedure: None; a historical body reference is not a direct relationship.
same_version_content_conflicts should fall from 14 to 0 for these cases
All fourteen PDFs remain; only seven manifest identities change.
